_doc: ANY% x WORLD: the act's shots (60 fps frames) and its subtitle lines, read by Act.tsx and prep/sponsors/world.py. Cue lists are frames inside the shot: cards (a card spawns), hits (a stamp or a line lands), cuts (a hard cut inside the shot), chirps, glitch (a screen comes up), typing ([from, to, step]: letters typing). The field shot is empty until built.json has WORLD ID clips; it then takes their length. Lines: at most 2.8 words a second.

lines.text: Fair question. World makes a ban land on a person, not a wallet.
Without World, a voided cheater makes a new wallet and comes back.
Again. And again. Each new account is free.
With World, one World ID gets one record book, once.
Then the same cheat fails the check, and the finding sticks.
The cheater's sales stop on every console.
New wallet, same person: same nullifier. Refused. The loop ends.
Games already fight this with hardware bans and phone numbers.
A bot's run is legal, so it replays perfectly.
So machines get an open tier, and humans get a human tier.
World doesn't detect bots. It caps each human at one record book.
Coaches pay runners for their ghosts.
One person, twenty wallets: twenty rows, twenty payment streams.
With World, they collapse to one.
Your coach agent wants to list your ghost for sale.
Nothing is listed until you approve it in World App.
At this event the identities are mock. In production, Orb-class.
